Your summary should consist of two parts, modifications in each file and their relationships.

From 1ab526d97a57e44d26fadcc0e9adeb9c0c0182f5 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Deepanshu Kartikey <kartikey406@gmail.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Dec 2025 06:53:54 +0530
Subject: [PATCH] net: nfc: fix deadlock between nfc_unregister_device and
 rfkill_fop_write

A deadlock can occur between nfc_unregister_device() and rfkill_fop_write()
due to lock ordering inversion between device_lock and rfkill_global_mutex.

The problematic lock order is:

Thread A (rfkill_fop_write):
  rfkill_fop_write()
    mutex_lock(&rfkill_global_mutex)
      rfkill_set_block()
        nfc_rfkill_set_block()
          nfc_dev_down()
            device_lock(&dev->dev)    <- waits for device_lock

Thread B (nfc_unregister_device):
  nfc_unregister_device()
    device_lock(&dev->dev)
      rfkill_unregister()
        mutex_lock(&rfkill_global_mutex)  <- waits for rfkill_global_mutex

This creates a classic ABBA deadlock scenario.

Fix this by moving rfkill_unregister() and rfkill_destroy() outside the
device_lock critical section. Store the rfkill pointer in a local variable
before releasing the lock, then call rfkill_unregister() after releasing
device_lock.

This change is safe because rfkill_fop_write() holds rfkill_global_mutex
while calling the rfkill callbacks, and rfkill_unregister() also acquires
rfkill_global_mutex before cleanup. Therefore, rfkill_unregister() will
wait for any ongoing callback to complete before proceeding, and
device_del() is only called after rfkill_unregister() returns, preventing
any use-after-free.

The similar lock ordering in nfc_register_device() (device_lock ->
rfkill_global_mutex via rfkill_register) is safe because during
registration the device is not yet in rfkill_list, so no concurrent
rfkill operations can occur on this device.

Fixes: 3e3b5dfcd16a ("NFC: reorder the logic in nfc_{un,}register_device")
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Reported-by: syzbot+4ef89409a235d804c6c2@syzkaller.appspotmail.com
Closes: https://syzkaller.appspot.com/bug?extid=4ef89409a235d804c6c2
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/all/20251217054908.178907-1-kartikey406@gmail.com/T/ [v1]
Signed-off-by: Deepanshu Kartikey <kartikey406@gmail.com>
Reviewed-by: Krzysztof Kozlowski <krzysztof.kozlowski@oss.qualcomm.com>
Link: https://patch.msgid.link/20251218012355.279940-1-kartikey406@gmail.com
Signed-off-by: Paolo Abeni <pabeni@redhat.com>

diff --git a/net/nfc/core.c b/net/nfc/core.c
index ae1c842f9c64..82f023f37754 100644
--- a/net/nfc/core.c
+++ b/net/nfc/core.c
@@ -1154,6 +1154,7 @@ EXPORT_SYMBOL(nfc_register_device);
 void nfc_unregister_device(struct nfc_dev *dev)
 {
 	int rc;
+	struct rfkill *rfk = NULL;
 
 	pr_debug("dev_name=%s\n", dev_name(&dev->dev));
 
@@ -1164,13 +1165,17 @@ void nfc_unregister_device(struct nfc_dev *dev)
 
 	device_lock(&dev->dev);
 	if (dev->rfkill) {
-		rfkill_unregister(dev->rfkill);
-		rfkill_destroy(dev->rfkill);
+		rfk = dev->rfkill;
 		dev->rfkill = NULL;
 	}
 	dev->shutting_down = true;
 	device_unlock(&dev->dev);
 
+	if (rfk) {
+		rfkill_unregister(rfk);
+		rfkill_destroy(rfk);
+	}
+
 	if (dev->ops->check_presence) {
 		timer_delete_sync(&dev->check_pres_timer);
 		cancel_work_sync(&dev->check_pres_work);
-- 
2.34.1

The patch addresses a deadlock between `nfc_unregister_device` and `rfkill_fop_write` by reordering lock acquisition. The modification is confined to a single file:

**File:** `net/nfc/core.c`  
**Function:** `nfc_unregister_device`

- Introduced a local variable `struct rfkill *rfk = NULL` to hold the device’s `rfkill` pointer temporarily.
- Inside the `device_lock(&dev->dev)` critical section, instead of directly calling `rfkill_unregister(dev->rfkill)` and `rfkill_destroy(dev->rfkill)`, the function now stores the pointer in `rfk`, sets `dev->rfkill = NULL`, and releases the lock.
- After `device_unlock(&dev->dev)`, the `rfkill` operations (`rfkill_unregister` and `rfkill_destroy`) are performed on the saved pointer, thereby avoiding the lock ordering inversion between `device_lock` and `rfkill_global_mutex`.

**Relationship:**  
The change resolves the ABBA deadlock by moving the acquisition of `rfkill_global_mutex` (via `rfkill_unregister`) outside the `device_lock` critical section. This ensures that the two locks are always taken in a consistent order, preventing circular wait. No other files are affected.
